learned_knowledge: LeagueLoop is a CustomTkinter borderless overlay that docks to the League of Legends client. It uses a background AutomationEngine running a WebSocket connection to LCU (League Client Update) APIs to automate actions like auto-accept, champion pick/ban, runes/skins configuration, and end-of-game honors.

concept: Riot Client Local API & DPAPI Encryption
learned_knowledge: RiotClientServices.exe runs a local API on 127.0.0.1. Port and token are extracted from active process cmdline args or lockfile at %LocalAppData%/Riot Games/Riot Client/Config/lockfile. It accepts PUT requests on /rso-authenticator/v1/authentication for login. Credentials in accounts.json are encrypted using Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI) CryptProtectData to tie them to the local Windows profile.

StatsScraper holds static hardcoded databases of champion win rates for different game modes (ARAM, Ranked, Arena, Quickplay). In the background, it runs a ThreadPoolExecutor to scrape live win rates from Lolalytics using BeautifulSoup, caching results for 30 minutes. If bs4 is missing or scraping fails, it falls back to the local database.

ToastManager handles non-blocking notifications container (pinned bottom-right). Single Toast instances have hover highlights and can spawn physics-based canvas particles (confetti) that drift down using gravity and air resistance simulations.

Unifies Riot Client and League Client scanning into a single, cached process scan pass. Reads RiotClientInstalls.json to resolve installation directories. If process cmdline is restricted by access permissions, reads the physical lockfiles directly from the resolved installation directories.

Allows selecting a default account stored in accounts.json. On application startup, if no client connection is detected, the application automatically launches the Riot Client using the resolved installation executable path and automates the RSO login macro for the default account.

When an active client session is detected, if the account's Riot ID or tagline is not found in the local database, a placeholder account entry is created with an empty password. In the UI, this displays as a warning button (⚠️ Update) which links directly to the credentials edit form.

Adding _EventBus.off(event_name, callback) allows dynamic components and UI widgets to safely clean up their event subscriptions, avoiding memory leaks and dangling callback execution when views are unmounted or re-rendered.

concept: BaseHTTPRequestHandler Test Harness for Local API
learned_knowledge: Testing standard library BaseHTTPRequestHandler implementations can be achieved cleanly without launching network sockets by creating an in-memory DummyAPIHandler subclass with BytesIO buffers for rfile and wfile and a MockServer object.

concept: Inertial Scroll Velocity Decay & Color Math Caching
learned_knowledge: Smooth scrolling in CTkScrollableFrame uses mousewheel delta normalized against speed multipliers and frame-by-frame exponential velocity decay (default 0.85). UI theme color utilities use functools.lru_cache for hex_to_rgb, interpolate_color, lighten_color, and darken_color to avoid main-thread string parsing bottlenecks during hover and press state re-renders.

concept: WAMP Anomaly Alerting & High-Resolution Splash Art Eviction
learned_knowledge: LCU WAMP event telemetry tracks event throughput (eps) alongside latency anomaly detection (>100ms threshold) and active event burst detection (>=25 eps or >=10 eps during anomaly). High-resolution splash art previews (1920x1080) are managed in a separate OrderedDict LRU memory cache with a max_splash_icons = 15 limit, allowing explicit eviction via evict_splash_art_memory() to manage RAM footprint during high champ select churn.

concept: Structured Health Monitoring & Priority Asset Queueing
learned_knowledge: The local REST server provides /healthz for detailed telemetry monitoring including uptime_seconds, lcu_connected status, automation loop state, and current LCU phase. AssetManager uses Python's queue.PriorityQueue to organize asynchronous worker thread jobs, allowing low-priority background preload tasks (priority 10) during champion select rolls without starving high-priority user interface image loads.

concept: WebSocket Exponential Jitter Backoff & Auto-Pruning Asset Caching
learned_knowledge: LCUClient WebSocket reconnects use exponential backoff (1s base up to 30s max) scaled by random jitter factor (0.8x-1.2x) to prevent thundering herd connections during LCU client restarts. AssetManager automatically evaluates disk cache file counts and total byte size during champion select asset pre-fetches, dynamically auto-pruning stale cache files when soft thresholds (350 files / 35MB) are breached.

concept: Connection Drop Diagnostics, Event Loop Telemetry & Theme RAM Optimization
learned_knowledge: LCUClient records connection drop history, timestamps, and failure reasons via _record_connection_drop(), alongside event loop dispatch latency tracking (_event_loop_latency_ms) and active connection uptime calculations. DesignTokens optimizes active UI theme memory using sys.intern string interning for token keys, values, and path components, providing optimize_theme_memory() and get_theme_memory_footprint() to prevent string object duplication in RAM.

concept: Dynamic Network Throttle, Pre-Serialized JSON & Adaptive HTTP Timeout
learned_knowledge: LCUClient uses dynamic network drop tracking within 15s windows to throttle rapid reconnect attempts when network adapters flap, while recording HTTP request latency histograms (_http_latency_samples, _http_latency_buckets) to dynamically adjust HTTP request timeouts based on p95 latency statistics. LeagueLoopAPIHandler uses static pre-serialized byte buffers (_HEALTH_OK_BYTES, _QUEUE_MODES_BYTES) for zero-allocation JSON responses, and AssetManager manages champion skin icon previews in a dedicated OrderedDict LRU memory cache with a max_skin_icons = 80 limit.
